correctness.rationale: Permutation symmetry reduces the complete two-shell first Walsh Gram matrix to ES=0 and ES^2=n for S=sum coordinates; positive masses on s and -t solve these exactly when st=n, with parity s=t=n mod2 and 1<=s,t<=n. Hence n odd or 4|n. The number of sample vertices is the sum of two binomial shell sizes, yielding the exact divisor minimum for all odd n. Independent exact binomial computation for each odd dimension up to 201 confirms first strict improvement at n=51, pair (3,17), 244362982488625 versus 247959266474053. The analytic all-n progression follows from the positive-polynomial identity for 3/4-R_(r+1)/R_r, whose numerator is 3(13r^4+65r^3+138r^2+144r+60); independently verified polynomially. Finite counts do not establish the infinite recurrence.
